claims.claim: Google pledged US$15b on 4 Nov and to pay 100% of its own power.
claims.source: Google announcement, 4 November 2026: https://blog.google/intl/en-my/company-news/inside-google/google-investment-malaysia-digital-infrastructure-november-2026/ ; Ministry of Higher Education account of the 4 November event, published 6 November 2026: https://www.mohe.gov.my/hebahan/sorotan-aktiviti/yb-menteri-kpt-hadiri-majlis-mantap-malaysia-bersama-ai-google-perkasa-pembangunan-bakat-digital-negara ; Prime Minister's speech, 4 November 2026: https://www.pmo.gov.my/ms/ucapanterkini/verbatim-text-yab-prime-minister-at-mantap-malaysia-bersama-ai-a-google-event/ .
claims.correction: Verified as an announced commitment. The investment period is 2027–2028. Paying campus electricity costs does not establish that every wider system or environmental cost is recovered.
claims.stale_check: The announcement predates the analysis's 7 November 2026 cutoff.

claims.claim: US$15b, 2027-2028; pays 100% of campus power and direct grid-connection costs

claims.correction: Preserve 'direct' when describing connection infrastructure costs. This verifies the company's pledge, not expenditure already completed.
claims.stale_check: Historical announcement verified as at the stated cutoff.

claims.claim: On 4 Nov, Google committed US$15b to data centres in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan
claims.source: Google announcement, 4 November 2026: https://blog.google/intl/en-my/company-news/inside-google/google-investment-malaysia-digital-infrastructure-november-2026/ ; Bernama, 4 November 2026: https://bernama.com/en/news.php?id=2630047 .
claims.correction: The announcement identifies planned campuses in those states and an operating Elmina campus. The US$15 billion programme also includes associated digital infrastructure and other initiatives; it is not described exclusively as building expenditure.
claims.stale_check: No subsequent change is needed to explain this qualification.

claims.claim: adding to 117 approved nationwide
claims.source: Google announcement, 4 November 2026: https://blog.google/intl/en-my/company-news/inside-google/google-investment-malaysia-digital-infrastructure-november-2026/ ; parliamentary record, 28 October 2026: https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-10-28?search=undefined .

claims.claim: Data centres: Malaysia wrote rules on who pays, and none on who gets heard
claims.source: Act 172, official reprint as at 1 June 2021, sections 12A–16, 21(6)–(7) and 23: https://planmalaysia.gov.my/planmalaysia/resources/dokumen/Akta_172/Act_172_Bersih_As_at_1st_June_2021.pdf ; EIA Order 2015, paragraph 3: https://www.doe.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Perintah-Kualiti-Alam-Sekeliling-Aktiviti-Yang-Ditetapkan-Eia-2015.pdf .
claims.correction: Existing law already provides participation procedures. The defensible criticism concerns gaps and conditions in project-specific participation, including the absence of a dedicated data-centre EIA entry.
claims.stale_check: These participation provisions substantially predate November 2026; this is not a stale correction caused by a recent reform.

claims.claim: Since 1 Aug 2025, data centres in the Peninsula and Labuan pay their own water tariff.
claims.source: Selangor Menteri Besar statement, 1 August 2025: https://content.airselangor.com/cmi-prod-blobstorageanon-001-sea/media/yotnscfj/mb-penyelarasan-tarif-air-202508.pdf ; Kelantan gazette P.U.(A) 226/2025, 30 July 2025: https://airkelantan.com.my/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/PERATURAN-PERATURAN-INDUSTRI-PERKHIDMATAN-AIR-NEGERI-KELANTAN-2025.pdf ; Air Kelantan implementation page: https://airkelantan.com.my/maklumat-pengguna/kadar-tarif/ .
claims.correction: A dedicated category exists, but universal actual billing from 1 August is not established. Selangor expressly deferred implementation to 1 September 2025. Kelantan's gazette commences on 1 August, whereas its operator page states 10 September. Distinguish statutory commencement from implementation.
claims.stale_check: The implementation differences arose in 2025 and were relevant before the analysis's cutoff.

claims.claim: separate data-centre water tariff RM5.30-5.38/m3, Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan
claims.source: SATU official statement, 2 August 2025: https://www.satuwater.com.my/v4/phocadownload/Kenyataan%20Media/Kenyataan%20Media%20SATU%202.pdf ; official tariff FAQ hosted by SAMB, 2025, question 6: https://samb.com.my/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/FAQ-Umum-TSM-TP2-Final.pdf .
claims.correction: The range has substantial support: SATU states a common RM5.30 base rate excluding electricity charges, and the FAQ gives a state-dependent electricity component of 0–8 sen/m3. That produces RM5.30–RM5.38 arithmetically. However, the original ministerial reply and direct confirmation of both endpoints across the applicable schedules were not obtained. Checked schedules independently confirm RM5.31 and RM5.32.
claims.stale_check: The uncertainty concerns complete primary-source coverage, not evidence that the range recently changed.

claims.claim: The Environmental Quality (Prescribed Activities) (Environmental Impact Assessment) Order 2015 (P.U.(A) 195/2015) sorts prescribed activities into two schedules.

claims.correction: The instrument number, title, structure and gazettal date are confirmed.
claims.stale_check: Verified against the original 2015 instrument.

claims.claim: Second Schedule activities, such as coal-fired power stations of 10MW or more, 'require public display and public comment' (para 3(3)).
claims.source: P.U.(A) 195/2015, paragraph 3(3) and Second Schedule item 11(a), 28 August 2015: https://www.doe.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Perintah-Kualiti-Alam-Sekeliling-Aktiviti-Yang-Ditetapkan-Eia-2015.pdf .
claims.correction: The threshold concerns construction of a coal-fired power station, with or without a transmission line.
claims.stale_check: The cited provision predates the analysis.

claims.claim: First Schedule activities, such as an industrial estate of 20 hectares or more, 'do not require public display and public comment unless otherwise instructed, in writing, by the Director General' (para 3(2)).
claims.source: P.U.(A) 195/2015, paragraph 3(2) and First Schedule item 17, 28 August 2015: https://www.doe.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Perintah-Kualiti-Alam-Sekeliling-Aktiviti-Yang-Ditetapkan-Eia-2015.pdf .
claims.correction: The prescribed activity is development of an industrial estate of at least 20 hectares. Campus size alone does not establish that classification.
claims.stale_check: The qualification follows the original wording.

claims.claim: Neither schedule contains a data-centre, computer or ICT entry.
claims.source: Both schedules of P.U.(A) 195/2015, 28 August 2015: https://www.doe.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Perintah-Kualiti-Alam-Sekeliling-Aktiviti-Yang-Ditetapkan-Eia-2015.pdf .
claims.correction: Verified for the inspected 2015 text. Absence of a dedicated entry does not exempt a project containing another prescribed activity.
claims.stale_check: The separate question of all subsequent amendments remains qualified below.

claims.claim: A campus enters the Order only as a 20-hectare 'industrial estate', a First Schedule category with no public display unless the Director General directs it.
claims.source: P.U.(A) 195/2015, both schedules: https://www.doe.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Perintah-Kualiti-Alam-Sekeliling-Aktiviti-Yang-Ditetapkan-Eia-2015.pdf ; DOE EIA Guideline in Malaysia 2016, section 4.1: https://www.doe.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/FA-EIA-GUIDELINE-IN-MALAYSIA-1.pdf .
claims.correction: Delete 'only'. Associated power generation, forest conversion, slope development or water infrastructure can trigger other categories when their conditions are met. DOE guidance applies Second Schedule treatment to a project containing a qualifying Second Schedule component.
claims.stale_check: These alternative triggers and guidance existed well before November 2026.

claims.claim: On 24 July 2026 Greenpeace Malaysia and co-signatories asked for data centres to be listed 'as a prescribed activity requiring a Schedule 2 Environmental Impact Assessment'.
claims.source: Original RimbaWatch and allies statement published by Greenpeace Malaysia, 24 July 2026: https://www.greenpeace.org/malaysia/press/83760/civil-society-calls-for-ban-on-data-centres-near-residential-areas/ ; named DagangNews report by Kamaliza Kamaruddin, 24 July 2026, separately checked against that statement: https://dagangnews.dagangnews.com/article/terkini/ngo-desak-kerajaan-sekat-pusat-data-berhampiran-kawasan-perumahan-72057 .
claims.correction: The date, quotation and address to DOE are confirmed. The original is attributed to RimbaWatch and allies, with Greenpeace among the endorsers. This verifies their request, not all factual assertions elsewhere in their statement.
claims.stale_check: Contemporaneous statement verified.

claims.claim: No amending order adding such an entry was found as of 7 Nov 2026.
claims.source: DOE's official order index: https://www.doe.gov.my/perintah/ ; NRES parliamentary answer, 10 December 2025, question 46: https://www.nres.gov.my/parlimen/Lists/papar-Jawapan-Parlimen.aspx?ID=++++2967 .

claims.stale_check: Currentness was specifically investigated; the exhaustive amendment check remains incomplete.

claims.claim: The PLANMalaysia data-centre planning guideline (Cabinet, 8 Oct 2024) lists DOE's environmental assessment among approvals but does not itself create an EIA trigger.
claims.source: Official PLANMalaysia Data Centre Planning Guidelines 2024, front matter and section 1.6: https://www.planmalaysia.gov.my/uploads/content-downloads/file_20251114204437.pdf ; statutory EIA Order 2015: https://www.doe.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Perintah-Kualiti-Alam-Sekeliling-Aktiviti-Yang-Ditetapkan-Eia-2015.pdf .
claims.correction: The Cabinet date is confirmed. Listing an assessment in planning guidance does not amend the statutory prescribed-activity schedules.
claims.stale_check: The later PDF upload date does not change the guideline's 2024 approval date.

claims.correction: The quotation and December 2024 reference date match. These are applications compared with capacity, not actual electricity use. Keep the historical date visible.

claims.source: Water Services Industry (Water Services Deposits, Fees and Charges) (Amendment) Regulations 2025, P.U.(A) 274/2025, gazetted 27 August and effective 1 September 2025: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/3046482/PUA%20274%20(2025).pdf ; Senate Hansard, 8 December 2025: https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/hindex/pdf/DN-08122025.pdf .

claims.claim: Planning permission is the local council's call.
claims.source: Act 172, sections 5, 21 and 22, official reprint as at 1 June 2021: https://planmalaysia.gov.my/planmalaysia/resources/dokumen/Akta_172/Act_172_Bersih_As_at_1st_June_2021.pdf .
claims.correction: Use 'local planning authority'. A council normally performs that role within its area, subject to statutory constraints and applicable state or national directions.

claims.claim: an application for planning permission 'shall be made to the local planning authority' (s21(1))
claims.source: Act 172, section 21(1), official reprint as at 1 June 2021: https://planmalaysia.gov.my/planmalaysia/resources/dokumen/Akta_172/Act_172_Bersih_As_at_1st_June_2021.pdf .
claims.correction: The section and quoted wording match.
claims.stale_check: The 2021 text is verified; targeted searches did not establish a later change to this provision.

claims.claim: Section 21(6) requires the authority to notify the owners of neighbouring lands of their right to object within 21 days, with a hearing on request (s21(7)), only 'if the proposed development is located in an area in respect of which no local plan exists'.
claims.source: Act 172, sections 21(6)–(8), official reprint as at 1 June 2021: https://planmalaysia.gov.my/planmalaysia/resources/dokumen/Akta_172/Act_172_Bersih_As_at_1st_June_2021.pdf .
claims.correction: The 21 days run from service. A qualifying objector must request the hearing when lodging the objection; the hearing follows within the statutory period.
claims.stale_check: The reprint was checked. A comprehensive post-2021 amendment audit remains incomplete.

claims.claim: Where a local plan exists, the public's formal objection point is the plan
claims.source: Act 172: https://planmalaysia.gov.my/planmalaysia/resources/dokumen/Akta_172/Act_172_Bersih_As_at_1st_June_2021.pdf ; MBPJ planning-permission checklist and public-notice template, 2018 edition: https://www.mbpj.gov.my/sites/default/files/mbpj/sumber/muat_turun_borang/borang-borang_online_unit_pusat_setempatosc/b02-proses_2-_borang_permohonan_km_skim-2018.pdf .

claims.claim: draft local plans and alterations must be advertised in three issues of at least two local newspapers, with not less than four weeks for objections (ss13(2), 16(3))
claims.source: Act 172, sections 13(2) and 16(3), official reprint as at 1 June 2021: https://planmalaysia.gov.my/planmalaysia/resources/dokumen/Akta_172/Act_172_Bersih_As_at_1st_June_2021.pdf .

claims.source: Act 172, sections 14(1) and 15(1), official reprint as at 1 June 2021: https://planmalaysia.gov.my/planmalaysia/resources/dokumen/Akta_172/Act_172_Bersih_As_at_1st_June_2021.pdf .

claims.claim: permission may not contravene the plan (s22(4)(a))
claims.source: Act 172, section 22(4)(a), official reprint as at 1 June 2021: https://planmalaysia.gov.my/planmalaysia/resources/dokumen/Akta_172/Act_172_Bersih_As_at_1st_June_2021.pdf .

claims.claim: The 2024 data-centre planning guideline sets 99-, 29-, 22- and 33-day tracks
claims.source: PLANMalaysia Data Centre Planning Guidelines 2024, processing methods and flowcharts: https://www.planmalaysia.gov.my/uploads/content-downloads/file_20251114204437.pdf .

claims.claim: its text shows no objection step

claims.claim: On 19 Oct 2026 the National Economic Action Council agreed to draft a Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill for Cabinet in 2027
claims.source: Secondary locator: Bernama, 19 October 2026: https://www.bernama.com/bm/news.php?id=2622567 ; corroborating government-media report published 20 October 2026: https://dewanekonomi.jendeladbp.my/2026/10/20/16174/ . omitted_facts: The EIA regime includes more than a campus-category test. DOE's 2016 guideline, section 4.1, addresses projects containing multiple prescribed activities and applies Second Schedule treatment when a qualifying component falls there. Paragraph 3(4) of the 2015 Order also addresses subdivision and expansion. Sources: https://www.doe.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/FA-EIA-GUIDELINE-IN-MALAYSIA-1.pdf ; https://www.doe.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Perintah-Kualiti-Alam-Sekeliling-Aktiviti-Yang-Ditetapkan-Eia-2015.pdf .

Planning-law geography matters. PLANMalaysia identifies separate planning legislation for Sabah, Sarawak and Kuala Lumpur. The Act 172 discussion should not be presented as an unqualified description of every Malaysian jurisdiction. Official overview: https://www.planmalaysia.gov.my/main/article/akta-172 .

Act 172 also provides publicity before draft-plan preparation under section 12A and an appeal route for qualifying section 21(6) objectors under section 23(1)(b). These strengthen the conclusion that existing law contains participation rights, although their coverage is conditional. Official reprint as at 1 June 2021: https://planmalaysia.gov.my/planmalaysia/resources/dokumen/Akta_172/Act_172_Bersih_As_at_1st_June_2021.pdf .

MBPJ's published 2018 planning checklist contains a project-notice template inviting neighbouring owners and others wishing to comment or object. It is evidence that published local procedures can extend beyond the analysis's simplified binary. It does not establish the exact legal basis of the July 2026 objection exercise. Source: https://www.mbpj.gov.my/sites/default/files/mbpj/sumber/muat_turun_borang/borang-borang_online_unit_pusat_setempatosc/b02-proses_2-_borang_permohonan_km_skim-2018.pdf .

The directly accessible 28 October 2026 answer gives August contracted demand of 2,346MW and actual use of approximately 1,374MW, or 58.5%. Those observations help distinguish current use from the much larger approval and eventual-completion figures. Source: https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-10-28?search=undefined .

Earlier official figures are not fully reconciled. On 15 October 2026 Johari described 57 existing data centres with 6,237MW, then said 6,230MW in the same answer, plus another 60 projects requiring 11,172MW. On 28 October he gave 55 operating within 117 and an eventual requirement of approximately 23,000–23,500MW. The later statement is preferable for reporting his latest stated position, but recency does not explain the changed classification or capacity basis. Do not infer closures, growth or an off-grid residual without reconciliation. Sources: https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-10-15 ; https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-10-28?search=undefined .

Water-demand guarantees supplement capital contributions. P.U.(A) 274/2025 inserts regulation 13A, requiring monthly demand estimates for the first six operating years, allowing revision after year three, and permitting a usage-guarantee charge when actual consumption falls short. The provision permits the charge; it does not prove universal collection. Gazette dated 27 August 2025, effective 1 September 2025: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/3046482/PUA%20274%20(2025).pdf .

The official water-tariff FAQ says catchment-conservation environmental costs were not yet included in TSM calculations because the implementation mechanism was still being refined. This limits any inference that the tariff already internalises every environmental cost. Source, question 11 notes: https://samb.com.my/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/FAQ-Umum-TSM-TP2-Final.pdf .

Public access and mandatory pre-approval comment are distinct. NRES announced access to executive summaries for both First and Second Schedule EIA reports from February 2025. That does not create the same mandatory public-comment requirement for every First Schedule project. Official statement, 22 January 2025: https://www.nres.gov.my/ms-my/pustakamedia/KenyataanMedia/PRESS%20STATEMENT%20PUBLIC%20ACCESS%20TO%20ENVIRONMENTAL%20IMPACT%20ASSESSMENT%20%28EIA%29%20REPORTS.pdf .

The US measures vary in effect. For example, Harwood's official proposal concerned additional review requirements for certain industrial development; rejecting it was not itself approval of a particular data centre. Ballotpedia and Redbud also use different inventories and classification procedures. Official Harwood ballot text: https://cityofharwood.com/documents/801/Home_Rule_Charter_Amendment001.pdf ; tracker methodology: https://datacentersontheballot.com/ .
source_assessment: The main bibliography identifies 17 distinct works when separately dated articles are counted separately: four legal or planning documents, one AMRO report, one Google announcement, one civil-society statement, eight articles across The Star, The Vibes, NST and W.Media, and two Ballotpedia reports. Redbud and an incompletely identified SAM submission add two ancillary references. The institutional range includes government, an intergovernmental economic body, business, civil society and journalism. That is meaningful breadth, but much of the journalism repeats the same ministerial answers, so article count overstates evidential independence. The original analysis lacks directly inspected written answers for several important figures, a reconciled project register, the original Kota Damansara case documents, and a complete set of official US election returns. Community views are largely mediated through news or NGOs. No distinct opposition-party source, independent planning-law analysis or relevant judgment is cited; political balance cannot be inferred merely from outlet names. Corporate and NGO originals establish what their authors announced or requested, not the truth of every underlying benefit or allegation. The 0.55 diversity estimate reflects this institutional breadth together with substantial primary-source and perspective gaps; it is a qualitative assessment, not a measured political-bias index.
overall_assessment: The analysis contains substantial accurate material: the Google announcement, AMRO's dated comparison, the principal statutory quotations, the Kelantan rate, the existence of utility cost-recovery mechanisms, and much of the ministerial project breakdown are supported. However, its central headline is false as an unqualified legal statement, and the 'only industrial estate' EIA claim is directly contradicted by the broader statutory scheme. Several shorter cards turn conditional participation rights into an unsupported claim that project-level participation is otherwise unavailable. Those errors were already present under the law and guidance available before the 7 November 2026 cutoff; they cannot be excused as stale criticism following a later reform. Other details remain unverified because the required originals were not obtained, especially certain written-answer figures, exact event attribution, the Bill timetable, the Kota withdrawal date and the complete US ballot tally. UNVERIFIED does not mean false. The 68/100 score is a qualitative editorial assessment weighted toward the central legal and numerical claims, not a statistical probability or a Dempster–Shafer combination of dependent sources. Repeated assertions have been consolidated where their factual content is identical; editorial recommendations, confidence labels, process self-descriptions and the proposed policy preference are not treated as independently provable external facts. The piece requires substantive revision before publication, chiefly to distinguish missing dedicated safeguards from the participation rules that already exist.
